Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/  skills/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for

  `$WORKSPACE_DIR/skills/<name>/scripts/`.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. The harness
  routes relative `write` and `edit` paths here automatically.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be

## Tool conventions

- Use `read` to consume input files (handles .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf, and
  plain text).
- Use the file-type skill manuals below to produce binary deliverables
  (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`

- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.

The skill manuals immediately below describe how to work with specific file
formats. Read them before tackling the task.


## Skill: docx

---
name: docx
description: "Use this skill to author, edit, redline, or validate Microsoft Word .docx files. Covers creating new documents from markdown or templates, editing existing documents in place, generating tracked-changes redlines, adding comments, and accepting/rejecting revisions. For READING existing .docx files, use the harness `read` tool — do not invoke this skill. Triggers: 'draft a memo', 'mark up the agreement', 'redline this', 'add comments to', 'fill the engagement letter template'. Does NOT apply to .pdf, .xlsx, .pptx, or .doc (legacy Word)."
---

# DOCX authoring, editing, redlining

> **Reading is not in scope.** To read an existing .docx, use the harness `read` tool. It already returns structured text via pandoc. This skill is for *writing*, *editing*, and *validating*.

## Quick reference

| Goal | Use |
|---|---|
| Generate a new doc from markdown | `scripts/generate_from_md.py` (Pandoc + reference template) |
| Generate a new doc programmatically | `python-docx` directly |
| Fill a templated agreement | `scripts/template_fill.py` (docxtpl / Jinja) |
| Edit an existing doc | `scripts/unpack.py` → mutate XML → `scripts/pack.py` |
| Produce a tracked-changes redline | `scripts/redline.py` |
| Add comments to a passage | `scripts/comments_add.py` |
| Accept all redlines | `scripts/accept_changes.py` |
| Validate a docx before delivery | `scripts/validate.py` (mandatory final step) |

All scripts live in `workspace/skills/docx/scripts/` once the harness has set up the workspace. Invoke them via `bash`.

## Creating a new document

Pick by what you have:

- **Markdown content + a styled firm template** → `generate_from_md.py input.md out.docx template.docx`. Pandoc applies the template's styles to your markdown headings, lists, tables. Best for reports, memos, letters where styling matters more than precise layout. Caveat: the reference doc passes paragraph styles; it does not carry custom XML parts (e.g., comment threads).
- **A template with named placeholders** → `template_fill.py template.docx context.json out.docx`. docxtpl renders Jinja2 expressions inside the template. Best for engagement letters, NDAs, structured agreements.
- **Programmatic build** → write Python using `python-docx`. Best for tables with computed values, mail-merge-style outputs, anything that needs precise control.

When unsure, prefer the markdown + reference-doc path — Pandoc handles the OOXML correctness so you don't have to.

## Editing an existing document

Three-step pattern:

```bash
python scripts/unpack.py input.docx workdir/
# edit XML files under workdir/word/
python scripts/pack.py workdir/ output.docx
python scripts/validate.py output.docx
```

Key files inside the unpacked tree:

- `word/document.xml` — body content (paragraphs, runs, tables)
- `word/styles.xml` — paragraph + run style definitions
- `word/numbering.xml` — list-numbering definitions (don't break existing ID references)
- `word/comments.xml` — comment thread content (created by `comments_add.py`)
- `word/header*.xml`, `word/footer*.xml` — running headers/footers
- `[Content_Types].xml` — MIME registration for every part. Edit when you add a new part type.
- `_rels/` and `word/_rels/` — relationships between parts. Edit when you reference a new image, comment, or external resource.

### Run-merging gotcha

Word writes adjacent runs (`<w:r>`) with identical formatting separately. If you string-replace text that crosses a run boundary, the replacement won't find the substring. `unpack.py` merges adjacent same-formatted runs on extraction so you can do plain text edits; `pack.py` is permissive about whatever run structure you write back.

### Smart-quote escaping

Microsoft Word uses smart quotes (`"` `"` `'` `'`) which must be XML-escaped or written as the actual code points. `unpack.py` substitutes them with XML entities for editing safety; `pack.py` reverses the substitution before zipping. Don't manually re-escape — let the scripts handle it.

### Whitespace preservation

Trailing whitespace inside `<w:t>` elements is significant. Both `unpack.py` and `pack.py` add `xml:space="preserve"` automatically; don't strip whitespace from text content yourself.

## Redlines (tracked changes)

```bash
python scripts/redline.py original.docx revised.docx redlined.docx \
  --author "Reviewer" --date "2026-04-30"
```

Default mode shells out to **Python-Redlines** (MIT) which compares the two documents and emits proper `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` revision elements. Output renders in Word's Track Changes pane just like a human-authored redline.

### Manual mode

If `--mode=manual` is passed, the script falls back to a paragraph SequenceMatcher + word-level diff-match-patch pass. Use this when:
- Python-Redlines fails on a particular doc structure (rare).
- You want to control which paragraphs are diffed.
- The change is purely formatting (`<w:rPrChange>` runs) rather than text.

### What gets tracked

- Insertions and deletions of text
- Insertions and deletions of paragraphs (deleted-whole-paragraph case requires `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>` or you get an empty paragraph after acceptance)
- Run-property changes via `<w:rPrChange>` (formatting-only revisions)

### What doesn't get tracked

- Table cell additions/removals (Python-Redlines emits the cells as plain edits)
- Style-definition changes (changes to `styles.xml` aren't revision-trackable)
- Image swaps

## Comments

```bash
python scripts/comments_add.py document.docx comments.json
```

`comments.json` is a list of `{anchor_text, author, comment}` objects. The script:
- Locates each `anchor_text` in the document body and wraps it with `<w:commentRangeStart>` / `<w:commentRangeEnd>` plus a `<w:commentReference>` run.
- Creates or appends to `word/comments.xml` (with proper id assignment).
- Patches `[Content_Types].xml` and `word/_rels/document.xml.rels` if commenting is being added for the first time.

Anchor matching is exact-string. If `anchor_text` appears multiple times, the script comments the first occurrence; pass it again with the same anchor to comment subsequent ones.

`<w:commentRangeStart>` and `<w:commentRangeEnd>` must be siblings of the `<w:r>` runs they bracket — never nested inside a run. If you write comments by hand, follow this rule.

## Accept / reject changes

```bash
python scripts/accept_changes.py redlined.docx accepted.docx
```

Uses LibreOffice headless via a documented StarBasic macro:

```basic
Sub AcceptAllRedlines() ThisComponent.AcceptAllRedlines() ThisComponent.store() End Sub
```

LibreOffice must be installed and on PATH (`soffice` binary). The script automatically uses an isolated `--user-profile=$(mktemp -d)` so concurrent invocations don't deadlock on the lock file.

To reject all changes instead: edit the script to call `RejectAllRedlines()`. To accept selectively: this isn't supported — open the doc in Word.

## Validation gate

**Always run `validate.py` before declaring the task complete.**

```bash
python scripts/validate.py output.docx
```

Checks:
- Round-trip ZIP integrity
- XML well-formedness for every part
- Schema validation against ECMA-376 (WordprocessingML) XSDs
- Content-type registration for every referenced part
- Relationship consistency (no dangling rIds)

Exit code 0 = valid. Non-zero exit code with line-number diagnostics = fix and re-pack.

## Common pitfalls

- **Legacy `.doc` (binary) is not supported.** Convert with `soffice --convert-to docx input.doc` first.
- **List numbering breaks after edits.** Numbering lives in `word/numbering.xml` keyed by `numId`. If you delete a list, also delete its numId reference; if you reorder, don't change IDs.
- **Headers and footers are separate parts** (`word/header1.xml`, etc.). Edits to body content don't touch them.
- **Pandoc reference-doc passes paragraph styles only.** Custom XML parts (comments, tracked changes baseline) are not carried over.
- **Don't pretty-print whitespace inside `<w:t>` elements.** Pretty-printing breaks runs that depend on exact spacing.
- **Tables: dual width specs.** Each cell needs both `columnWidths` (in `<w:tblGrid>`) and per-cell `<w:tcW w:type="dxa">`. Percentages (`pct`) render fine in Word but break in Google Docs.

## Out of scope

- Reading: use the `read` tool.
- Producing PDFs from .docx: pipe through `soffice --convert-to pdf` after this skill is done.
- Signing / encryption / DRM.
- Word macros (`.docm` with VBA).

For READING existing .pptx files, use the harness `read` tool — do not invoke this skill. Triggers: 'build a deck', 'create slides', 'edit slide N', 'add a chart slide'. # PPTX authoring and editing

> **Reading is not in scope.** To read an existing .pptx, use the harness `read` tool (markitdown extracts slide text). This skill is for *writing* and *editing*.

## Quick reference

| Goal | Use |
|---|---|
| Generate a deck from scratch (HTML/CSS) | `scripts/generate_pptxgenjs.js` |
| Generate a deck from markdown | `scripts/generate_marp.sh` |
| Build slides programmatically | `python-pptx` directly |
| Edit a shape on an existing slide | `scripts/edit_shape.py` (JSON patch) |
| Add or remove a slide | unpack → edit → pack |
| QA a deck deterministically | `scripts/deterministic_qa.py` |
| Validate before delivery | `scripts/validate.py` |

## Generation modalities

**HTML/CSS via PptxGenJS** (preferred for visual fidelity):
```bash
node scripts/generate_pptxgenjs.js deck.json out.pptx
```
`deck.json` describes slides as a JSON tree; the script invokes PptxGenJS (and html2pptx for HTML inputs) to produce a fully-editable .pptx. Best for branded decks with gradients, custom fonts, complex shapes.

**Markdown via Marp**:
```bash
bash scripts/generate_marp.sh deck.md out.pptx
```
Best for content-heavy decks (lectures, reports) where markdown is more natural than JSON.

**Programmatic via python-pptx**:
Best when shapes are computed (e.g., one slide per data row). Requires manual EMU positioning.

## Editing existing decks

Three-step pattern, like docx:
```bash
python scripts/unpack.py input.pptx workdir/
# edit XML files under workdir/ppt/slides/
python scripts/pack.py workdir/ output.pptx
python scripts/validate.py output.pptx
```

For surgical shape edits without unpacking, use `edit_shape.py`:
```bash
python scripts/edit_shape.py input.pptx \
  --slide 2 --shape "Title 1" --op set_text --value "New title"
```

JSON patch ops: `set_text`, `set_position` (EMU), `set_size`, `recolor`, `delete`.

## OOXML gotchas specific to pptx

- **Use `defusedxml.minidom`, NOT `xml.etree.ElementTree`.** ElementTree corrupts presentation namespaces during round-tripping. `unpack.py` and `pack.py` use minidom; if you write your own XML manipulation, do the same.
- **EMU units everywhere.** 1 inch = 914400 EMU. Slide positions, sizes, font sizes (in pt × 100) all use derived EMU values.
- **Placeholders vs free shapes.** Placeholders inherit from slide masters; free shapes don't. Editing a placeholder's text is `<a:t>` content; editing its layout requires master-slide changes.
- **Don't pretty-print pptx XML on pack.** Whitespace-significant runs (`<a:r>`) break if reformatted. `pack.py` preserves the original whitespace.
- **Slide cloning is more than a file copy.** Use `unpack` + `pack` — manual file copies miss the rIds in `_rels/` and the `Content_Types.xml` registration.

## Deterministic QA loop

After every generation, run:

```bash
python scripts/thumbnail.py deck.pptx thumbs/   # PDF + JPEGs per slide
python scripts/deterministic_qa.py deck.pptx > qa.json
```

`deterministic_qa.py` checks:
- Shape bounding boxes don't extend past slide edges
- No two shapes overlap with > 50% area intersection
- Font sizes ≥ 11pt for body text, ≥ 18pt for titles
- All placeholders are filled (no `Click to add title` defaults)
- Bullet lists don't exceed 7 items per slide

Output is JSON listing each violation with slide number and shape id. Fix violations and re-render.

(A vision-model QA pass is intentionally out of scope for v1. Add `--use-vision` later if deterministic checks miss layout issues.)

## Validation gate

**Always run `validate.py` before declaring done.** Schema-validates against ECMA-376 PresentationML XSDs, checks rId consistency, content-type registration.

## Out of scope

- Reading: use the `read` tool.
- SmartArt creation (limited python-pptx support).
- Complex embedded charts beyond what python-pptx exposes.
- Slide transitions / animations (rarely matter for legal output).
- Vision-model layout review (deferred to v2).



## Skill: xlsx

description: "Use this skill to author or edit Microsoft Excel .xlsx files. Covers building workbooks with formulas, editing existing files, recalculating formulas, and scanning for #REF!/#DIV/0!/#VALUE! errors. For READING existing .xlsx files, use the harness `read` tool — do not invoke this skill. Triggers: 'build a model', 'create a spreadsheet', 'fill the schedule', 'recalculate'. Does NOT apply to .pdf, .docx, .pptx, or .xls (legacy Excel)."
---

# XLSX authoring and editing

> **Reading is not in scope.** To read an existing .xlsx, use the harness `read` tool (pandas extracts every sheet as a markdown table). This skill is for *writing*, *editing*, and *recalculating*.

## Quick reference

| Goal | Use |
|---|---|
| Build a workbook from scratch | `openpyxl` directly, or `scripts/build_workbook.py` for banker conventions |
| Edit cells in an existing file | `openpyxl.load_workbook(...)` → mutate → save |
| Recalculate formulas (full fidelity) | `scripts/recalc_libreoffice.py` |
| Recalculate formulas (no LibreOffice) | `scripts/recalc_pure_python.py` |
| Scan for formula errors | `scripts/scan_errors.py` |
| Validate before delivery | `scripts/validate.py` |

## Banker conventions (mandatory for financial models)

Apply these to every workbook unless the task explicitly overrides:

- **Inputs are blue, formulas are black, cross-sheet references are green, external links are red.** Use `Font(color='0000FF')` etc.
- **Negatives in parentheses, not minus signs.** Use number format `#,##0;(#,##0)`.
- **Red negatives in P&L tables.** Use `#,##0;[Red](#,##0)`.
- **Accounting format for currency.** `_-* #,##0_-;-* #,##0_-;_-* "-"_-;_-@_-` (or the localized equivalent).
- **Multiples shown as `0.0x`**, not `0.0` followed by an "x" character. Format: `0.0"x"`.
- **Underline-only on totals**, not bold-and-underline. Use `Border(bottom=Side(style='thin'))`.
- **No merged cells in input ranges.** Merged cells break formulas that reference them; reserve merging for headers and titles only.
- **Units in adjacent cells**, not in the cell with the value. `($M)` next to the value, not `"$1,234M"` as a string.

`scripts/build_workbook.py` applies these conventions automatically given a JSON spec.

## Formula authoring

- **Always emit formulas, never calculated values.** If the user wants `revenue × growth`, write `=B2*C2`, not `1234.56`. The recalc step materializes values.
- **Use named ranges** for cross-sheet inputs. `wb.defined_names["assumptions"] = DefinedName(...)`. Easier to audit.
- **Document units in adjacent cells** so the model is self-explanatory.
- **No volatile functions in hot paths.** `OFFSET`, `INDIRECT`, `NOW`, `TODAY` recalculate on every change and slow large workbooks.

## Recalculation — choose your engine

`openpyxl` writes formula *strings*; it does not evaluate them. You must recalculate before delivery, otherwise consumers will see `=B2*C2` literal text where they expect numbers (in some readers) or stale cached values (in others).

**LibreOffice path** (`recalc_libreoffice.py`) — ground truth:
```bash
python scripts/recalc_libreoffice.py input.xlsx output.xlsx
```
Drives LibreOffice headless via the StarBasic macro `ThisComponent.calculateAll(); ThisComponent.store()`. Slow (~5–10s per workbook) but matches Excel for nearly every function. Use this when the workbook contains modern Excel features.

**Pure-Python path** (`recalc_pure_python.py`) — fast, partial:
```bash
python scripts/recalc_pure_python.py input.xlsx output.xlsx
```
Uses `xlcalculator` to evaluate every formula in pure Python. Fast (~0.5s per workbook). Covers ~80% of common functions: arithmetic, `SUM`, `IF`, `VLOOKUP`, `INDEX`/`MATCH`, basic string/date functions.

**Does NOT support**: `XLOOKUP`, `LET`, dynamic arrays (`FILTER`, `SEQUENCE`, `UNIQUE`), `LAMBDA`, `BYROW`, `TEXTJOIN` with refs, structured table references, most modern (post-2019) Excel features.

If you used any of those, run the LibreOffice path. The pure-Python path is for CI environments without LibreOffice.

## Error scan

After every recalc, scan for formula errors:

```bash
python scripts/scan_errors.py output.xlsx > errors.json
```

Reports every cell whose computed value matches `#REF!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#VALUE!`, `#NAME?`, `#NULL!`, `#NUM!`, or `#N/A`. Output is JSONL with `{sheet, address, value}` per line.

If errors exist, fix and re-recalc. Don't ship a workbook with `#REF!`s — it's the most common reason a deliverable fails QA.

## Validation gate

`scripts/validate.py output.xlsx` schema-validates against ECMA-376 SpreadsheetML XSDs and confirms ZIP integrity, content-type registration, sheet relationships.

## Out of scope

- Reading: use the `read` tool.
- **PivotTables** — `openpyxl` round-trips existing pivots but cannot create or modify them. If a task requires pivot creation, escalate (Windows-only via COM, not portable).
- **DAX measures and Power Pivot** — `openpyxl` can't write these. Same limitation.
- **VBA macros (`.xlsm`)** — out of scope for this skill. Macros require Excel runtime.
- **Conditional formatting beyond simple cell-value rules** — `openpyxl` supports basic CF; complex rules (top-N, data bars across sheets) often fail to round-trip.
- **Charts beyond the python-pptx-equivalent set** — line/bar/scatter work; combo charts and trendlines round-trip unreliably.

The Trustee shall have **specific and express authority** to make elections under **IRC §643(e)(3)**, which permits the fiduciary of a trust to elect to recognize gain or loss on the distribution of property in kind to a beneficiary, as if the property had been sold to the beneficiary at its fair market value. This election can be an important tax planning tool --- for example, it may allow the trust to recognize losses on depreciated assets or to shift gain recognition in a tax-efficient manner --- and the Trustee needs express authority to utilize it. **Please specifically reference IRC §643(e)(3) by section number in the tax provisions article of the trust. Do not rely on general tax election language alone.** General boilerplate language authorizing the Trustee to make \"all available tax elections\" may not be sufficient to clearly authorize this specific election, and we want to eliminate any ambiguity.

**[D. Payment of Taxes]{.underline}**

All estate taxes, inheritance taxes, and other death taxes, if any, attributable to assets passing under the trust or the pour-over will shall be paid from the residuary estate before division into shares, unless otherwise required by applicable tax apportionment statutes. The Trustee shall have authority to make all decisions regarding the allocation and apportionment of taxes among the various assets and beneficiaries of the estate, consistent with applicable law.

**[E. Generation-Skipping Transfer Tax]{.underline}**

Include standard generation-skipping transfer (GST) tax provisions and allocations in the trust. The Grandchildren\'s Education Trust described in Section IX involves transfers to skip persons (grandchildren) and may implicate the GST tax. Include appropriate language authorizing the Trustee to allocate Peggy\'s GST exemption to the Grandchildren\'s Education Trust and to any other transfers that may be subject to GST tax, in a manner that minimizes the overall GST tax burden on the estate and its beneficiaries.

**[F. Income Tax Reporting]{.underline}**

During Peggy\'s lifetime, the trust is a grantor trust under IRC §§671--679, and all trust income, deductions, and credits are reported on Peggy\'s individual income tax return (Form 1040). After Peggy\'s death, the trust becomes irrevocable and the trust (and any sub-trusts, including the Sophia Davenport-Chen Protected Trust and the Grandchildren\'s Education Trusts) will file separate fiduciary income tax returns (Form 1041).

**[XIV. Additional Provisions and Drafting Notes]{.underline}**

The following additional provisions should be included in the trust agreement. These are largely standard provisions, but please ensure they are present and properly drafted.

**Governing Law.** All trust and will provisions shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the **State of California**, without regard to conflict of laws principles.

**Severability.** Include a standard severability clause providing that if any provision of the trust is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect to the maximum extent permitted by law.

**Headings.** Article and section headings are included for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the interpretation or construction of any provision of the trust.

**Definitions.** Include a definitions article at the beginning of the trust agreement defining key terms used throughout the document, including but not limited to: \"Beneficiary,\" \"Descendants\" (define to include legally adopted persons), \"Education Expenses,\" \"Incapacity,\" \"Trustee,\" \"Trust Protector,\" \"Per Stirpes,\" and other terms of art. Ensure the definitions are consistent throughout the trust and will.

**Perpetuities Savings Clause.** Include a standard perpetuities savings clause consistent with California\'s Rule Against Perpetuities. Under California Probate Code §21205, a trust created on or after January 1, 2016 is subject to a **90-year vesting period**. Include a provision stating that, notwithstanding any other provision of the trust, all trust interests must vest no later than 90 years after the date of the trust\'s creation, and that any interest that has not vested by that date shall be distributed outright to the then-living beneficiaries of the trust in such shares as the Trustee determines are most consistent with Peggy\'s overall estate planning intent.

**Revocation and Amendment.** Peggy retains full power to amend or revoke the trust at any time during her lifetime, provided she has capacity to do so. Any amendment must be in writing, signed by Peggy, and delivered to the Trustee (or, if Peggy is serving as Trustee, retained in the trust records). No amendment shall require the consent of any beneficiary or other person.

**Irrevocability Upon Death.** The trust becomes irrevocable upon Peggy\'s death. After Peggy\'s death, no person shall have the power to amend, revoke, or terminate the trust (except as expressly provided in the trust\'s terms regarding the Trust Protector\'s limited powers and the termination provisions of the sub-trusts).

**Counterparts and Execution.** The trust agreement shall be executed in duplicate originals. Provide for notarized execution and witness attestation in accordance with California law. Include appropriate signature blocks for Peggy as both Settlor and initial Trustee, and include an acknowledgment form for notarization.

**Exhibit A --- Jewelry Appraisal Schedule.** Prepare a placeholder page for Exhibit A, which will contain the detailed jewelry appraisal schedule to be completed and attached before execution. Label the placeholder clearly and include a note indicating that the exhibit will be incorporated upon attachment.

**Schedule of Trust Assets.** Prepare a schedule listing all assets to be transferred to and funded into the trust, as described in Section III above. This schedule should be attached to the trust agreement and updated at the time of funding.

**[XV. Assets Excluded from This Engagement]{.underline}**

For clarity, and to help avoid drafting errors, the following assets are **NOT** part of this trust engagement and should **NOT** be addressed in the trust agreement or the pour-over will:

**1. Individual Retirement Account.** Peggy\'s IRA at Pinnacle Wealth Management (Account #PWM-IRA-6619, current FMV approximately \$2,400,000) is not part of the trust corpus and passes by beneficiary designation, not by the terms of the trust or will. Beneficiary designations for the IRA are being handled separately through a companion letter to Pinnacle Wealth Management. Do not include any provision in the trust or will that purports to govern, direct, or influence the disposition of the IRA.

**2. Life Insurance (ILIT).** Pacific Guardian Life Insurance Policy #PGL-5571002 (death benefit of \$1,000,000) is owned by the Davenport-Chen Insurance Trust dated April 2, 2016 (the ILIT), which is a separate irrevocable trust that is not being modified in this engagement. Because the policy is owned by the ILIT and not by Peggy individually, it is not part of Peggy\'s probate estate or trust estate. Do not address the ILIT or the life insurance policy in the trust agreement or the pour-over will.

If you have questions about the interplay between these excluded assets and the new trust --- for example, regarding coordination of IRA beneficiary designations with the trust\'s distribution scheme --- please come see me before you begin drafting so we can discuss.

**[XVI. Closing Instructions and Timeline]{.underline}**

**[A. Deliverables]{.underline}**

Please prepare the following two documents:

> 1\. **The Margaret Davenport-Chen Revocable Trust dated January 15, 2025** --- a complete trust agreement including all articles, definitions, exhibits (including a placeholder for Exhibit A --- Jewelry Appraisal Schedule), and the Schedule of Trust Assets.
>
> 2\. **Pour-Over Last Will and Testament of Margaret Davenport-Chen** --- a complete pour-over will incorporating all provisions described in Section XII above, including executor nominations, the pour-over provision, guardian nominations (both primary and contingent), the specific disinheritance clause, and the revocation of prior instruments.

**[B. Deadline]{.underline}**

First drafts of both documents must be on my desk no later than **January 10, 2025**. This gives us five calendar days before the target execution date of January 15, 2025, which should be sufficient for my review, at least one round of revisions, and transmittal to Peggy for her review and approval before the execution ceremony.

**[C. Review Process]{.underline}**

I will review both documents carefully against these instructions and the client file before sending the drafts to Peggy. Plan for at least one round of revisions based on my comments, and possibly a second round after Peggy reviews the documents. Build this into your schedule.

**[D. Questions and Ambiguities]{.underline}**

If any instruction in this memorandum is unclear, or if you identify any potential issues --- whether tax, fiduciary, interpretive, or otherwise --- please schedule time with me to discuss before you complete the drafts. **Do not make assumptions.** If something is ambiguous, flag it. I would rather answer a question now than correct an error in a draft.

**[E. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

These instructions and all drafts prepared pursuant to them are privileged and confidential attorney work product. Do not circulate these instructions or any drafts outside the Trusts & Estates practice group without my prior written approval.

This summary memorializes background information gathered during three meetings with the client held on November 18, November 25, and December 4, 2024, and is intended to provide context for the drafting team. **This document is NOT an instruction document.** Detailed drafting instructions will follow in a separate memorandum addressed to the assigned associate.

Our client is **Margaret \"Peggy\" Davenport-Chen**, age 71, a United States citizen domiciled in California. Peggy resides at 418 Birchwood Lane, Atherton, CA 94027. Her estimated gross estate is approximately **\$23.7 million** (excluding assets held in the existing irrevocable life insurance trust). She has three adult children and two grandchildren. **[2. Family Members and Dynamics]{.underline}**

**2.1 Dr. David Chen (Son, Age 47)**

David is Peggy\'s eldest child, age 47, and a cardiologist at Stanford Medical Center. He is married to **Jennifer Chen** (née Watkins), and together they have two minor children: **Lily Chen** (age 12, born June 3, 2012) and **Marcus Chen** (age 9, born November 17, 2015). The family resides in Palo Alto, California.

Peggy describes David as \"the responsible one.\" He is financially stable, conservative in temperament, and well-organized. After Raymond\'s death, David stepped in to help Peggy manage Raymond\'s medical practice closure, final tax filings, and the administrative burdens of the existing estate plan. Peggy trusts David\'s judgment implicitly and views him as the natural choice for fiduciary roles.

Jennifer is a devoted mother, and Peggy has a warm, close relationship with her daughter-in-law. Peggy considers Jennifer an excellent parent and indicated that Jennifer would be her first choice as guardian for any minor grandchildren if the need arose.

Peggy is especially close to her granddaughter Lily, who has shown a strong aptitude for music --- specifically piano --- and who Peggy says \"has Raymond\'s musical ear.\" This is relevant to a specific personal property bequest discussed in Section 3 below. Peggy wants David as her first successor trustee and executor due to his reliability and sound judgment.

Peggy has emphasized repeatedly that she and Raymond always prioritized education, and she wants to ensure that the grandchildren\'s educational expenses are comprehensively provided for.

**2.2 Sophia Davenport-Chen (Daughter, Age 44)**

Sophia is Peggy\'s middle child, age 44, born October 8, 1980. She is an executive director of the **Bay Area Youth Alliance**, a nonprofit organization serving at-risk youth in the San Francisco area. She is unmarried and has no children. She resides in San Francisco, California.

This subsection requires particular attention from the drafting team. Sophia has a history of financial difficulties. She filed for **Chapter 7 bankruptcy**, which was **discharged in 2018**. The bankruptcy resulted from a combination of accumulated credit card debt, a failed small business venture (a retail boutique), and remaining student loan obligations from graduate school.

Peggy loves Sophia deeply but was candid and direct about her concerns during our meetings. In her words: \"Sophia has a big heart but has never been good with money.\" Peggy does not want Sophia to receive a large lump-sum distribution that could be mismanaged or exposed to future creditors.

Peggy was **explicit** that she does **not** want Sophia serving as a trustee in any capacity --- not as primary trustee, successor trustee, or co-trustee --- for any trust under this estate plan. Peggy stated: \"Sophia should not be in charge of money --- hers or anyone else\'s.\" This exclusion is rooted in concern about Sophia\'s financial track record, not any doubt about her moral character.

Peggy wants Sophia\'s share held in a protective spendthrift trust with distributions at the trustee\'s discretion for health, education, maintenance, and support. The trust should terminate when Sophia reaches **age 60** (i.e., October 8, 2040), at which point Peggy hopes Sophia will have developed greater financial maturity. Peggy specifically requested this sub-trust be named the **\"Sophia Davenport-Chen Protected Trust.\"**

Despite the financial concerns, Peggy wants Sophia to receive a **meaningful and generous** share of the estate. Peggy indicated Sophia\'s share should be **larger than Tommy\'s** to account for the fact that Sophia has no spouse\'s income to rely on and works in the comparatively lower-paying nonprofit sector.

**2.3 Thomas \"Tommy\" Davenport-Chen (Son, Age 39)**

Tommy is Peggy\'s youngest child, age 39, and works as a freelance documentary filmmaker. He is married to **Ricardo Esteban Morales**. They have no children currently but have expressed interest in adopting in the future. They reside in Portland, Oregon.

Peggy describes Tommy as \"creative, passionate, and finding his way.\" His income is irregular given the nature of freelance documentary work, but Peggy does not view him as irresponsible with money --- merely in an industry that does not provide consistent earnings.

Peggy wants Tommy to receive the **Tahoe vacation home** outright. Tommy and Ricardo spent many summers there with Raymond, and the property carries deep sentimental value. Total gross estate (excluding ILIT): approximately **\$23,700,000**.

Reconciliation: \$6,800,000 + \$1,900,000 + \$7,200,000 + \$3,570,000 + \$2,400,000 + \$890,000 + \$940,000 = **\$23,700,000**.

**[4. Estate Planning Goals and Motivations]{.underline}**

**4.1 Primary Objectives**

Based on our three meetings, Peggy articulated the following estate planning goals:

> • **Replace the existing 2016 estate plan entirely.** All prior wills and trust instruments, other than the ILIT, should be revoked and superseded.

>
> • **Honor Raymond\'s memory** through the **Raymond and Margaret Chen Scholarship Fund** at Stanford University, Fund ID #SU-RMCSF-2022. Peggy was emphatic that the scholarship bear **both** their names. She became visibly emotional discussing this goal and considers it a central legacy of the estate plan.

**[5. Additional Notes and Considerations]{.underline}**

Peggy is mentally sharp, fully engaged, and demonstrates complete competency. I have no concerns whatsoever about her current capacity to execute estate planning documents.

Peggy intends to **fund the trust promptly** after execution with all non-retirement, non-ILIT assets. A **pour-over will** should be prepared to capture any assets not transferred to the trust during her lifetime.

The Trust Protector shall exercise the foregoing powers in good faith and with due regard for the Settlor\'s intent as expressed in this Trust Agreement. The Trust Protector shall not be liable to any person for any action taken or not taken in good faith in the exercise of the powers granted under this Section.

**Section 10.3 --- Successor Trust Protector**

If Martin Fairchild is unable or unwilling to serve as Trust Protector, or if he ceases to serve for any reason after having commenced service, a majority of the then-current adult beneficiaries of this Trust (determined as of the time such appointment is to be made) may appoint a successor Trust Protector by written instrument delivered to the then-acting Trustee. Any successor Trust Protector shall be an independent person or professional (i.e., not a beneficiary of this Trust and not related by blood or marriage to any beneficiary of this Trust). If the adult beneficiaries are unable to agree upon a successor Trust Protector within sixty (60) days after a vacancy arises, any beneficiary may petition a court of competent jurisdiction to appoint a successor Trust Protector.

**[ARTICLE XI --- TAX PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Tax Elections Generally**

The Trustee is directed to make such tax elections and allocations as the Trustee, in the Trustee\'s sole discretion, deems advisable to minimize the overall estate, gift, generation-skipping transfer, and income tax burden on the Trust Estate and its beneficiaries. The Trustee is authorized to make elections under the Internal Revenue Code, the California Revenue and Taxation Code, and any other applicable federal, state, or local tax laws. The Trustee may allocate receipts and disbursements between income and principal in such manner as the Trustee deems equitable and consistent with the Uniform Principal and Income Act, as adopted in California. The Trustee shall have the authority to file all required tax returns, pay all taxes due, contest any tax assessment or deficiency, and take all other actions that the Trustee deems appropriate in connection with any tax matter affecting the Trust Estate or any beneficiary thereof.

**Section 11.2 --- Estate Tax Apportionment**

Unless otherwise required by applicable law, all estate, inheritance, generation-skipping transfer, and similar death taxes attributable to assets of the Trust Estate or passing under this Trust Agreement shall be apportioned among and paid from the Residuary Estate. Specific bequests of real property, personal property, and cash under Article VII shall not bear any portion of such taxes unless the Residuary Estate is insufficient to pay such taxes in full, in which case such taxes shall be apportioned among the specific bequests in the reverse order of abatement set forth in Section 7.5 above. The Trustee shall not seek reimbursement or contribution from any beneficiary of a non-probate asset (such as the proceeds of a life insurance policy or a retirement account) for any taxes attributable to such asset, unless the Trustee determines that such reimbursement or contribution is required by law.

**Section 11.3 --- Portability**

The Trustee acknowledges that the Settlor\'s estate may be eligible for the deceased spousal unused exclusion (\"DSUE\") amount pursuant to Internal Revenue Code §2010(c)(4) by reason of the death of the Settlor\'s predeceased spouse, Dr. Raymond Chen, on March 14, 2021. The Trustee is authorized and directed to cooperate with the executor of the Settlor\'s estate, if any, in taking all steps necessary to preserve and utilize any available DSUE amount for the benefit of the Trust Estate and its beneficiaries. This Trust is structured so that the Settlor\'s estate may qualify for any applicable portability election under the Internal Revenue Code.

**Section 11.4 --- Grantor Trust Status**

During the Settlor\'s lifetime, this Trust shall be treated as a \"grantor trust\" for federal and state income tax purposes under Internal Revenue Code §§671 through 679. The Settlor shall be treated as the owner of the Trust for income tax purposes and shall report all items of income, deduction, and credit of the Trust on the Settlor\'s individual income tax returns. The Trust shall not be required to file a separate income tax return during the Settlor\'s lifetime, except as may be required by applicable law or regulation. Upon the Settlor\'s death, the Trust shall become a separate taxpayer for income tax purposes, and the Trustee shall obtain a taxpayer identification number for the Trust and file all required income tax returns.

**[ARTICLE XII --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- Governing Law**

This Trust Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to principles of conflicts of law that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. The situs of the Trust shall be the State of California, and any court of competent jurisdiction in the State of California shall have jurisdiction over all matters relating to the administration of this Trust.

**Section 12.2 --- Severability**

If any provision of this Trust Agreement, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable for any reason, the remaining provisions of this Trust Agreement shall continue in full force and effect and shall not be affected, impaired, or invalidated thereby. The invalid provision shall be modified or reformed to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid and enforceable while preserving the Settlor\'s original intent as closely as possible.

**Section 12.3 --- Headings**

The article headings, section headings, and other captions used in this Trust Agreement are for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the meaning, interpretation, or construction of any provision of this Trust Agreement.

**Section 12.4 --- Gender and Number**

Wherever used in this Trust Agreement, the singular shall include the plural, the plural shall include the singular, and the masculine gender shall include the feminine and neuter genders, and vice versa, unless the context clearly requires otherwise.

**Section 12.5 --- Counterparts**

This Trust Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

**Section 12.6 --- Perpetuities Savings Clause**

Notwithstanding any other provision of this Trust Agreement, all trusts created hereunder (including, without limitation, the Sophia Davenport-Chen Protected Trust created under Section 8.4) shall terminate no later than twenty-one (21) years after the death of the last survivor of the Settlor and the beneficiaries named herein who are living on the date of this Trust Agreement. Upon such termination, if any trust has not previously terminated in accordance with its specific terms, the Trustee shall distribute the remaining trust assets, including accumulated income, to the then-current income beneficiaries of such trust in proportion to their respective interests, outright and free of trust. This provision is intended to comply with the common law rule against perpetuities and any applicable statutory modifications thereto.

**Section 12.7 --- Entire Agreement**

This Trust Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Settlor and the Trustee regarding the creation, administration, and distribution of the Trust Estate and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, trust instruments, and amendments, whether oral or written, relating to the subject matter hereof. No prior revocable trust agreement, declaration of trust, or amendment thereto executed by the Settlor shall have any force or effect after the execution of this Trust Agreement.

**Section 12.8 --- Notices**

All notices, requests, demands, consents, and other communications required or permitted under this Trust Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when (a) delivered personally; (b) sent by United States certified or registered mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or (c) sent by nationally recognized overnight courier service. Such communications shall be addressed to the parties at the addresses set forth in this Trust Agreement, or at such other addresses as any party may designate by written notice to the other parties in accordance with this Section. Notices to the Trustee shall be delivered to the Trustee\'s address as set forth in Section 3.2 hereof or as updated by the Trustee in writing.

**[ARTICLE XIII --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

For purposes of this Trust Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below, unless the context clearly requires otherwise:

**\"Beneficiary\"** shall mean any person or entity entitled to receive, or who is receiving, distributions of income or principal under this Trust Agreement, whether such distributions are mandatory or discretionary, and whether such person\'s interest is vested or contingent. The term \"beneficiary\" shall include both current beneficiaries and remainder beneficiaries of any trust created hereunder.

**\"Children\" or \"Child\"** shall mean the Settlor\'s biological children: Dr. David Chen, Sophia Davenport-Chen, and Thomas \"Tommy\" Davenport-Chen. The term \"children\" shall also include any child born to or legally adopted by the Settlor after the date of this Trust Agreement, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise.

**\"Descendants\"** shall mean all children, grandchildren, and more remote lineal descendants of the referenced person, in all generations, including persons who have been legally adopted by the referenced person or by any descendant of the referenced person. For purposes of this definition, a legally adopted person shall be treated as a natural child of the adopting parent and shall not be treated as a descendant of the person\'s biological parents, except as otherwise required by applicable law.

**\"Education\"** (for purposes of the health, education, maintenance, and support standard used herein) shall be broadly construed to include tuition, fees, books, supplies, room and board, transportation, and related expenses incurred in connection with attendance at any accredited primary, secondary, college, university, graduate, or professional educational institution, as well as vocational and trade schools, tutoring, educational travel, and continuing education programs.

**\"Incapacity\" or \"Incapacitated\"** shall have the meaning set forth in Article V of this Trust Agreement.

**\"Per Stirpes\"** shall mean distribution by right of representation as defined in California Probate Code §240, meaning that if a beneficiary predeceases the Settlor or otherwise fails to survive to the date of distribution, such beneficiary\'s share shall be distributed to such beneficiary\'s then-living descendants, divided at each generation so that each branch of the family receives an equal share.

**\"Residuary Estate\"** shall have the meaning set forth in Section 8.1 of Article VIII of this Trust Agreement.

**\"Trust Estate\"** shall mean all property, of every kind and description, held under this Trust Agreement from time to time, including the original trust corpus described in Schedule A, all additions thereto, and all earnings, profits, increments, proceeds, and reinvestments thereof, less any distributions, payments, or charges properly made against the Trust Estate.

**\"Trustee\"** shall mean the individual or entity serving as Trustee of this Trust at any given time, whether the initial Trustee or any successor Trustee appointed in accordance with Article III of this Trust Agreement. When used in the plural, \"Trustees\" shall mean all persons or entities then serving as Trustee.

**LAST WILL AND TESTAMENT** **OF** **MARGARET DAVENPORT-CHEN**

 

I, **MARGARET DAVENPORT-CHEN**, also known as Margaret Chen, also known as Peggy Davenport-Chen, a resident of 418 Birchwood Lane, Atherton, California 94027, County of San Mateo, State of California, being of sound mind and memory and not acting under duress, menace, fraud, or the undue influence of any person, do hereby make, publish, and declare this to be my Last Will and Testament.

This instrument is executed as a pour-over will in conjunction with that certain revocable inter vivos trust known as The Margaret Davenport-Chen Revocable Trust, dated January 15, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as the \"Trust\"), of which I am the Settlor and initial Trustee. It is my intention that this Will and the Trust together constitute my comprehensive estate plan, and that the provisions herein be read and construed in harmony with the provisions of the Trust.

I declare that I am a widow. My beloved husband, Dr. Raymond Chen, passed away on March 14, 2021. I have three (3) living adult children, namely:

> \(a\) **Dr. David Chen**, age forty-seven (47), currently residing in Palo Alto, California;
>
> \(b\) **Sophia Davenport-Chen**, age forty-four (44), currently residing in San Francisco, California; and
>
> \(c\) **Thomas \"Tommy\" Davenport-Chen**, age thirty-nine (39), currently residing in Portland, Oregon.

I further declare that I have two (2) grandchildren, both of whom are minor children of my son Dr. David Chen and his wife Jennifer Chen (née Watkins), namely:

> \(a\) **Lily Chen**, born June 3, 2012; and
>
> \(b\) **Marcus Chen**, born November 17, 2015.

I make this Will freely and voluntarily, and I have carefully considered the disposition of my estate as set forth herein and in the Trust.

**[ARTICLE I --- REVOCATION OF PRIOR WILLS]{.underline}**

I hereby revoke all prior wills and codicils heretofore made by me. This Last Will and Testament entirely replaces and supersedes any prior testamentary instruments previously executed by me, including, without limitation, any will or codicil executed in connection with my prior estate plan dated in or about 2016, and any and all amendments, modifications, or supplements thereto. This instrument, together with the Trust, constitutes the sole expression of my testamentary intent.

**[ARTICLE II --- FAMILY DECLARATIONS]{.underline}**

For the purpose of identification and to avoid ambiguity, I declare the following with respect to my family:

**Section 2.1 --- Deceased Spouse.** My husband, Dr. Raymond Chen, predeceased me, having died on March 14, 2021. All references to my husband or to Dr. Raymond Chen in this Will or in any prior testamentary instrument are references to my deceased spouse.

**Section 2.2 --- Children.** I have three (3) living children: Dr. David Chen, Sophia Davenport-Chen, and Thomas \"Tommy\" Davenport-Chen. References herein to my \"children\" refer exclusively to these three individuals.

**Section 2.3 --- Grandchildren.** I have two (2) grandchildren: Lily Chen, born June 3, 2012, and Marcus Chen, born November 17, 2015. Both are the children of my son Dr. David Chen and his wife Jennifer Chen (née Watkins).

**Section 2.4 --- Children\'s Spouses.** My son Dr. David Chen is married to Jennifer Chen (née Watkins) of Palo Alto, California. My son Thomas \"Tommy\" Davenport-Chen is married to Ricardo Esteban Morales of Portland, Oregon.

**Section 2.5 --- Sibling.** My sister, Eleanor Davenport, resides in Scottsdale, Arizona.

**[ARTICLE III --- POUR-OVER PROVISION]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Pour-Over Distribution.** I hereby direct that all property of my estate, whether real, personal, or mixed, wherever situated, that is subject to this Will and that does not otherwise pass by specific bequest, joint tenancy, beneficiary designation, or other operation of law, shall be distributed to the then-acting Trustee of The Margaret Davenport-Chen Revocable Trust, dated January 15, 2025, as said Trust may be amended from time to time prior to my death, to be added to the trust estate and to be held, administered, and distributed by the Trustee in accordance with the terms and provisions of said Trust, including any amendments thereto made prior to my death. This pour-over provision is made pursuant to California Probate Code Section 6300 and the provisions of Division 6, Part 1 of the California Probate Code, as they may be amended from time to time.

**Section 3.2 --- Invalid or Unenforceable Trust.** In the event that the Trust is, for any reason whatsoever, held to be invalid, unenforceable, revoked, or inoperative, in whole or in part, by a court of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law, then the property that would otherwise have been distributed to the Trustee pursuant to Section 3.1 of this Article shall instead be held, administered, and distributed as if the terms and provisions of the Trust as they existed on the date of this Will were incorporated into and set forth in this Will in their entirety. In such event, the Executor shall serve as Trustee of such testamentary trust and shall be vested with all powers, duties, and discretions granted to the Trustee under the terms of the Trust.

**Section 3.3 --- Lapsed or Failed Bequests.** This pour-over provision shall apply to all probate assets not otherwise specifically disposed of by this Will, including, without limitation, any lapsed, failed, or otherwise ineffective bequests, devises, or dispositions under this Will. Any such property shall be distributed to the then-acting Trustee of the Trust in accordance with Section 3.1 of this Article.

**Section 3.4 --- Coordination with Trust.** The Executor shall cooperate and coordinate with the Trustee of the Trust to ensure the orderly and efficient administration and distribution of my estate in accordance with my overall estate plan as expressed in this Will and in the Trust.

**[ARTICLE IV --- NOMINATION OF EXECUTOR]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Primary Executor.** I hereby nominate and appoint my son, Dr. David Chen, currently residing in Palo Alto, California, as Executor of this Will.

**Section 4.2 --- Successor Executor.** In the event that Dr. David Chen is unable or unwilling to serve as Executor, or having commenced service, ceases to serve for any reason, I hereby nominate and appoint Broadleaf Fiduciary Services, Inc., a California corporation with principal offices at 200 California Street, Suite 1050, San Francisco, California 94111, as successor Executor of this Will.

**Section 4.3 --- Powers of Executor.** I grant to any Executor serving hereunder full power and authority under the California Independent Administration of Estates Act, California Probate Code Section 10400 et seq., including full authority to administer my estate without court supervision to the maximum extent permitted by law. The Executor shall have the power to sell, lease, mortgage, exchange, pledge, or otherwise deal with any and all estate property, whether real, personal, or mixed, as the Executor deems advisable for the proper administration of my estate, all without the necessity of obtaining prior court approval except as required by law. The Executor may, in the Executor\'s sole discretion, petition the court for full or limited authority under the Act. The Executor shall further have all powers granted to executors and personal representatives under Division 7 of the California Probate Code, as they may be amended from time to time.

**Section 4.4 --- Bond Waiver.** I request that no bond or other security be required of any Executor nominated herein, whether serving in an individual capacity or in a corporate fiduciary capacity. If the court or applicable law nevertheless requires a bond, I direct that the bond be set at the minimum amount permitted by law.

**Section 4.5 --- Executor Compensation.** Any Executor serving hereunder shall be entitled to reasonable compensation for services rendered in connection with the administration of my estate, as provided under California Probate Code Section 10800 et seq. In the event that Broadleaf Fiduciary Services, Inc. serves as Executor, it shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with its published fee schedule in effect at the time of service, which compensation shall be in lieu of, and not in addition to, the statutory compensation otherwise available under the California Probate Code.

**[ARTICLE V --- NOMINATION OF GUARDIAN FOR MINOR GRANDCHILDREN]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Guardian of the Person.** In the event that any minor grandchild of mine is in my care or custody at the time of my death, or in the event that a guardian of the person of any such minor grandchild is required to be appointed, I hereby nominate and appoint Jennifer Chen (née Watkins) of Palo Alto, California, as guardian of the person of such minor grandchild or grandchildren. I have given careful consideration to this nomination and believe that Jennifer Chen will provide a loving, stable, and nurturing home environment for my grandchildren.

**Section 5.2 --- Guardian\'s Authority.** The appointed guardian shall have the care, custody, and control of the person of any such minor grandchild, with all powers and duties provided by law, including those set forth in Division 4 of the California Probate Code. The guardian shall provide for the health, education, and general welfare of the minor grandchild in a manner consistent with my values and wishes, and shall make decisions regarding the child\'s upbringing, schooling, medical care, and religious instruction as the guardian deems to be in the best interests of the child.

**Section 5.3 --- Bond Waiver for Guardian.** I request that no bond or other security be required of any guardian nominated herein. If the court or applicable law nevertheless requires a bond, I direct that the bond be set at the minimum amount permitted by law.

**[ARTICLE VI --- PAYMENT OF DEBTS, EXPENSES, AND TAXES]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Debts and Expenses.** I direct my Executor to pay from my estate all of my legally enforceable debts, expenses of my last illness, reasonable funeral and burial expenses, and all costs and expenses of the administration of my estate, in each case as and to the extent required by applicable law. I do not, by this direction, intend to revive any obligation barred by the applicable statute of limitations or to impose any obligation upon my Executor to pay any debt that is not legally enforceable. My Executor shall use reasonable judgment in determining the validity and enforceability of any claim against my estate and may, in the Executor\'s discretion, contest, compromise, settle, or otherwise resolve any such claim.

**Section 6.2 --- Taxes.** I direct that all estate, inheritance, generation-skipping transfer, and other death taxes (including interest and penalties thereon) attributable to property passing under this Will, under the Trust, or by reason of my death, whether or not such property is part of my probate estate, shall be apportioned and paid in accordance with the tax apportionment provisions of the Trust. To the extent that the Trust does not address the apportionment of any particular tax or to the extent that the Trust\'s tax apportionment provisions are held to be invalid or unenforceable, such taxes shall be apportioned in accordance with California Probate Code Section 20110 et seq. I direct my Executor to coordinate with the Trustee of the Trust regarding all tax elections, filings, returns, and related matters, and to make such elections as will, in the judgment of the Executor and the Trustee, minimize the overall tax burden on my estate and on the Trust to the greatest extent practicable.

**Section 6.3 --- No Exoneration.** Unless otherwise specifically provided in the Trust or elsewhere in this Will, no specific devise of real or personal property made hereunder shall be exonerated from any mortgage, deed of trust, security interest, lien, or other encumbrance existing at the time of my death. Any such encumbered property shall pass subject to any such mortgage, deed of trust, security interest, lien, or other encumbrance, and the beneficiary receiving such property shall take it subject to all such obligations without right of reimbursement from my general estate.

**[ARTICLE VII --- SIMULTANEOUS DEATH / SURVIVAL REQUIREMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Survivorship Requirement.** If any beneficiary under this Will does not survive me by thirty (30) days, such beneficiary shall be deemed to have predeceased me for all purposes of this Will, and all provisions of this Will shall be construed accordingly. This thirty-day survival requirement shall apply to all gifts, bequests, devises, and dispositions made under this Will, unless a different survival period is expressly provided with respect to a particular provision.

**Section 7.2 --- Statutory Survival Provisions.** The thirty-day survival period set forth in Section 7.1 is intended to supplement, and not to replace, the applicable statutory survival requirements under California Probate Code Section 6211 (relating to simultaneous death) and Section 21109 (relating to the one-hundred-twenty-hour survival requirement), to the extent that the thirty-day period is more restrictive than such statutory requirements. In the event that the thirty-day survival period set forth herein is held to be invalid or unenforceable for any reason, the applicable statutory survival period shall control.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- NO-CONTEST CLAUSE]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- No-Contest Provision.** If any beneficiary under this Will shall, directly or indirectly, contest or attack this Will or any provision hereof, or the Trust or any provision thereof, or any other instrument, document, or transaction related to my estate plan, or shall seek to impair, invalidate, or set aside any of the provisions hereof or thereof, or shall conspire with, assist, or encourage any other person to do any of the foregoing acts, then in each such case, such beneficiary shall forfeit his or her entire interest under this Will, and such forfeited interest shall be distributed among the remaining non-contesting beneficiaries of this Will and the Trust in proportion to their respective interests, as if such contesting beneficiary had predeceased me without surviving issue.

**Section 8.2 --- Scope of No-Contest Provision.** This no-contest provision is intended to be enforceable to the maximum extent permitted by applicable California law. It is my express desire and intent that any person who challenges my estate plan in any manner whatsoever shall receive nothing from my estate. I have been advised regarding the legal implications of this provision and have included it after careful deliberation and with full knowledge of its consequences.

**[ARTICLE IX --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Governing Law.** This Will shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to principles of conflicts of law. All questions concerning the validity, construction, and administration of this Will shall be determined by reference to California law, and any proceedings related to this Will or to the administration of my estate shall be commenced and maintained in the Superior Court of the State of California for the County of San Mateo.

**Section 9.2 --- Severability.** If any provision of this Will, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Will or the application of such provision to other persons or circumstances, and the remaining provisions of this Will shall continue in full force and effect. It is my intent that the provisions of this Will be construed and enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law.

**Section 9.3 --- Headings.** The article and section headings contained in this Will are included solely for convenience of reference and shall not affect the meaning, interpretation, or construction of any provision of this Will. In the event of any conflict between a heading and the substantive text of a provision, the substantive text shall control.

**Section 9.4 --- Definitions.** As used in this Will, the following terms shall have the following meanings:

> \(a\) The term \"Executor\" shall mean and include any Executor or successor Executor serving hereunder from time to time.
>
> \(b\) The term \"Trust\" shall mean and refer to The Margaret Davenport-Chen Revocable Trust, dated January 15, 2025, as it may be amended, restated, or supplemented from time to time prior to my death.
>
> \(c\) The term \"Trustee\" shall mean and refer to the then-acting trustee or co-trustees of the Trust.
>
> \(d\) The term \"my estate\" shall mean and refer to all property, whether real, personal, or mixed, wherever situated, owned by me at the time of my death or in which I have any interest at the time of my death, that is subject to disposition under this Will.

**Section 9.5 --- Gender and Number.** Whenever used in this Will, words of any gender shall be deemed to include every other gender, and words used in the singular number shall include the plural, and words used in the plural number shall include the singular, as the context may require. The use of the masculine, feminine, or neuter pronoun shall not be deemed to be a limitation, and any such pronoun shall be construed to include all genders.
